covered_actors: Providers of general-purpose AI models placed on the Union market (including providers of models released under free and open-source licenses)
Downstream entities modifying existing general-purpose AI models such that they become providers
Authorised representatives of general-purpose AI model providers established outside the Union

evidence.quote: Article 53(1)(d) AI Act requires all providers of general-purpose AI models to draw up and make publicly available a sufficiently detailed public summary of the content used for the training of the model (the ‘Summary’), according to a template provided by the AI Office (the ‘Template’).

Describe the measures implemented before model training to respect reservations of rights from the TDM exception or limitation before and during data collection, including the opt-out protocols and solutions honoured by the provider or, as applicable, by third parties from which datasets have been obtained:
evidence.source_section: Annex 3.1. Respect of reservation of rights from text and data mining exception or limitation

evidence.quote: Providers of all general-purpose AI models placed on the Union market must fulfil the above obligation, including providers of general-purpose AI models released under free and open-source licenses4, in so far as the models fall within the scope of the AI Act5.
4 The exception for free and open-source general-purpose AI model under Article 53(2) AI Act does not apply to the obligation to make publicly available the Summary.

Authorised representative name and contact details:
Only applicable if the provider is established outside the Union (see Article 54 AI Act).
Non-compliance may be sanctioned with fines of up to 3% of the provider’s annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher.

The AI Office may verify whether the Template has been filled in correctly in order to assess if the provider has complied with Article 53(1)(d) AI Act. In this context, the AI Office has all enforcement powers under the AI Act and and may request corrective measures.
The supervision and enforcement by the AI Office for compliance with the rules for general-purpose AI models will start as of 2 August 2026.
evidence.source_section: 8. Entry into application of the obligation and special rules for models placed on the market before 2 August 2025 (33)

compliance_deadlines: 2025-08-02: Obligation under Article 53(1)(d) AI Act to make the public summary of training content publicly available enters into application for general-purpose AI models placed on the Union market
2026-08-02: AI Office supervision and enforcement powers for compliance with general-purpose AI model rules begin
2027-08-02: Deadline for providers of general-purpose AI models placed on the Union market before 2 August 2025 to make the corresponding Summary publicly available

Every six months (or sooner if additional training data requires a materially significant update): Required update frequency for the Summary when a marketed model is further trained on additional data
penalties_summary: The AI Office holds all enforcement powers under the AI Act, may request corrective measures, and may sanction non-compliance with fines of up to 3% of the provider's annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15,000,000, whichever is higher.
implementation_notes: Commission Communication C(2025) 8311 final setting out an Explanatory Notice and standardized Template implementing the binding obligation in Article 53(1)(d) of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act). The free and open-source exception in Article 53(2) does not apply to this summary obligation. SMEs/start-ups have a proportional cap for scraped domain disclosure (top 5% or 1,000 domains, whichever is lower, versus top 10% for other providers). The AI Office verifies proper completion without conducting work-by-work checks; the Commission intends to publish the Template as an online form and may review it before 2 August 2026.
